name: AWS lightweight formal methods (ShardStore reference models, P and PObserve)
subject: Amazon S3 ShardStore storage node (Rust) and AWS distributed protocol designs (e.g. S3 strong consistency) with log conformance via PObserve
tool: Rust executable reference models + property-based testing, Loom, Shuttle, Miri, Crux, Prusti (early); P checker and PObserve
org: Amazon Web Services (with UT Austin, ETH Zurich, UW co-authors)
toolchain: Rust toolchain (ShardStore, Shuttle); .NET P compiler/checker; Java PObserve

tcb.unverified_translator: reference models, test generators and biasing, coarse crash-state generation, in-memory disk, Loom bounds, Shuttle randomness, Crux size bound; PObserve log parser and timestamp ordering

pattern: small same-language executable reference model reused as mock + randomized differential conformance testing, crash-state generation and stateless model checking; P design models checked against service logs

property_notes.liveness: narrow: ShardStore forward progress after clean shutdown and deadlock detection by stateless model checking
property_notes.parsing: Crux bounded proof of deserialiser panic-freedom up to a size bound; S3 messaging-protocol parsing not validated
property_notes.refinement: property-based tests framed by authors as refinement; no proof
property_notes.trace-validation: PObserve post-hoc log monitoring against P specs
property_notes.ai_provenance: CLAUDE.md in p-org/P only; nothing on ShardStore
